audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and packet both said Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie.
audit.why: Galio's kit past level 3 buys durability and team utility; Annie's stun-into-burst is the only lane kill threat, which is what a 52.22% win rate over 1103 games reflects.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side aligned to the content/packet chart with ratings following.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes said Galio's ultimate is 'a roam/peel tool' without the number that makes that actionable.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s with a 4000-5500 range — the longest cooldown either champion has, and the reason his level 6 barely touches the lane.
audit.corrected: 180 seconds stated in phases[4].why and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) whys[0], early and spikes[0] all refer to 'Galio's passive shield' — his passive is Colossal Smash, an empowered area basic attack, not a shield. (b) The auto-reset tell was absent entirely. (c) Nothing on the page mentioned the taunt, which is the ability that actually decides whether Annie escapes.
audit.why: Riot text: passive is 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area'. Shield of Durand (W, 18/17/16/15/14s, 275 range) is the defensive stance that taunts on release. missingInteractions flags the auto-reset tell on Colossal Smash. Annie has no dash, so a taunt into Justice Punch's knockup is the whole death pattern.
audit.corrected: Shield of Durand named as the stance and taunt; Colossal Smash written in as the wind-up tell in dosFull[1].d; taunt added to enemyWin and dontsFull[0].d.
sources: ownerKit — no dash on any slot

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's derived flags put 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' on Justice Punch, and missingInteractions builds a 'terrain-cuts-retreat' item on top of it.
audit.why: Riot's description of Justice Punch is a step-back charge that knocks up the first enemy champion encountered — no terrain is created. Per the instruction to trust the description over a misfiring flag, no terrain claim was written.
audit.corrected: The underlying true half was kept — you have no dash, so Flash is reserved for his knockup, not for damage — and written into breakdown.feeding without asserting terrain.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are close and mechanical — Galio's passive shield absorbs some of your burst, but your stun still punishes bad positioning, so whoever plays cleaner wins these trades. Through level 3 it stays skill-dependent: his Q poke adds up but doesn't threaten a kill alone, and your Pyromania stun can turn a poke exchange into a real trade if you time your engage right. Play patiently and look to punish his cooldowns rather than force fights blindly.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are close and mechanical — Shield of Durand's stance blunts some of your burst, but your stun still punishes bad positioning, so whoever plays cleaner wins these trades. Through level 3 it stays skill-dependent: Winds of War adds up from 825 but never threatens a kill alone, and Pyromania turns a poke exchange into a real trade if you time the engage. Punish his cooldowns rather than force fights blindly.

edits.before: Annie's burst combo continues to threaten a one-shot on squishy targets throughout the game, while Galio's itemization leans into tankiness and taunt-lockdown for his team rather than personal kill pressure. Respect his ultimate as a teamfight-swinging tool that can lock down your whole team, but in isolated skirmishes your stun-Tibbers combo remains the scarier immediate threat. Play around vision so Galio can't flash-ult onto you unseen.
edits.after: Annie's burst still threatens a one-shot on squishy targets all game, while Galio's itemization leans into resistances and taunt lockdown for his team rather than personal kill pressure. Respect Hero's Entrance as a teamfight swing — he lands on an ally, shields them, and knocks your group up — but in isolated skirmishes your stun-Tibbers stays the scarier threat. Track where his allies are, because that is where he can arrive.

edits.before: Farm safely behind his shield and poke with Q
edits.after: Poke with Winds of War from 825 range

notes: Packet defect confirmed: no Galio ability was named anywhere. All five now appear. Repeated factual error corrected in three places: 'Galio's passive shield' — the passive is Colossal Smash, an empowered area auto; the defensive stance is Shield of Durand (W). Derived-flag error: Justice Punch carries a 'terrain: creates terrain' flag that Riot's description does not support, so the 'terrain-cuts-retreat' missing-interaction was written in only for its true half (Annie has no dash, so Flash answers the knockup).
